about.heading: Who Am I?
about.paragraph1: I'm a Full-Stack Software Engineer focused on Product, specialized in building solutions that solve real user pain points and streamline complex operations. I have 5+ years of experience across the full software development lifecycle, from discovery and architecture to implementation, testing, deployment and observability.
about.paragraph2: I currently work at Shopee as a Software Engineer, building technology for large-scale logistics and customs operations, including the Customs Clearance Platform, integrating Siscomex and J.P. Morgan, which contributed to RioGaleão's operation receiving the Logistics Excellence Program Award, processing 2M+ records and 100K+ invoices per day. I'm particularly interested in distributed systems, developer productivity, observability and AI-powered engineering.
about.paragraph3: I belive that innovation isn't necessarily creating something new and from scratch. If we facilitate the life of at least one person this will already be innovation.

palpite.title: Palpite!
palpite.description: A social prediction platform for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with groups, live rankings and AI match analysis.
palpite.problem: Friends who want to compete on match predictions usually rely on spreadsheets and chat messages, with no real-time ranking or shared experience.
palpite.solution: I built mobile (React Native, Expo) and web (React, Vite) apps on Supabase, a Go backend with WebSocket and Redis for real-time rankings, and a Python/FastAPI service using scikit-learn and the Gemini API for natural-language match analysis.
palpite.result: A full-stack platform where users create prediction groups, compete with virtual Palpicoins, challenge friends and follow live rankings.

juscash.title: JusCash - DJE Publications Automation
juscash.description: An automation system that collects and organizes publications from São Paulo's Electronic Justice Gazette (DJE), built as a technical case.
juscash.problem: Reviewing judicial publications by hand is slow and error-prone, and there was no central place to track their status.
juscash.solution: I built a Python scraper that collects DJE publications into the database, a Node.js/Prisma API documented with Swagger, and a Next.js frontend (TailwindCSS, Shadcn) with authentication, filters, detail modals and a Kanban board.
juscash.result: An end-to-end flow from scraping to review, where publications are searched and moved across Kanban stages.

sgr.title: SGR - Revenue Management System
sgr.description: A web system to control orders and payments at charity events, built by a team of six as an Integrator Project at Univesp for a real client, Obra Social Célio Lemos.
sgr.problem: The organization controlled orders and payments manually during charity events, which caused errors and made financial closing harder.
sgr.solution: Together with a team of six, I built a responsive Next.js interface for mobile and tablet, with PostgreSQL on Neon for cloud storage and CI/CD on Vercel.
sgr.result: A deployed system that automates order and payment control and supports financial reporting for the organization.

geo.title: Satellite Imagery Geoprocessing Web Portal
geo.description: A satellite imagery geoprocessing web portal, built as a team Integrator Project at Fatec for a real client, Visiona.
geo.problem: Remote sensing professionals needed a simple way to search, visualize and download public satellite imagery, without dealing directly with geospatial data APIs.
geo.solution: I built the frontend with React, TypeScript and Leaflet for the map interface (pan/zoom), integrated with a Python backend that processes imagery (NumPy, OpenCV) and queries AWS's public satellite catalogs via STAC. The team worked across 4 Scrum sprints.
geo.result: A working portal that lets users search, manipulate and download multi-band satellite imagery directly from the browser.

stats.title: Statistical Analysis Web Portal
stats.description: A statistical analysis platform for electoral data, built as a team Integrator Project at Fatec for a real client, the TV Vanguarda network, to be used by its journalists.
stats.problem: Journalists needed to explore electoral data from five municipalities in the Paraíba Valley without relying on manual spreadsheets, with charts that were easy to read and export.
stats.solution: I processed and cleaned the data with Python and Pandas in Jupyter Notebooks, generating interactive Plotly charts (bar, pie, donut) embedded directly into an HTML/CSS/JavaScript frontend, without a traditional API layer between them. When regional data wasn't available for smaller municipalities, we adapted the scope to city-level analysis.
stats.result: An interactive platform where journalists explore data by city and export the charts as PNG.
